input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale:
Section 7.2 (the first clause numbered 7.2) conditions our ability to engage another provider on first disclosing and matching any more favourable offer for Vendor — a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal binding Customer for the whole term, with no defined product category, no 12-month limit and no exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. It therefore fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. The repair changes only the mandatory operator so that no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer, leaving the negated mechanics and every other word intact; exclusivity running in our favour is untouched.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.82

ops.oldText: Customer must disclose and match for Vendor
ops.newText: Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We changed the mandatory operator in Section 7.2 so that we are not required to disclose or match competing offers before engaging another provider; as drafted it was an open-ended right of first refusal and de facto exclusivity on us, and it contradicted Section 12.3, where Cobalt acknowledges we have given no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Flip Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation into an express absence of any exclusivity/ROFR duty on Customer.
